newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Swiss list prompts look at Israel accounts.
newsitem.headline: Swiss list prompts look at Israel accounts.

text.p: Israel said on Friday it would publish lists of unclaimed properties and accounts in the face of charges that it, like Switzerland, held assets of Jews killed in the Nazi Holocaust.
Swiss banks on Tuesday unveiled a list of pre-1945 account holders who may have been among the six million Jews perished during the World War Two Holocaust.

On Friday, Professor Yossi Katz of Tel Aviv's Bar Ilan University told Israel Radio the Jewish state's Custodian General presided over a number of such accounts which could total as much as $70 million in today's dollars.
Swiss bankers have said the total amount found in dormant Swiss accounts opened by foreigners before the end of the war was around $40.5 million.

"It (Israel's Custodian General) has not located the owners according to the lists in its hands. It has also not published -- something that was done two days ago by the Swiss has not been done by the State of Israel -- the custodian has not published until today details on the property and deposits," Katz said.
Etty Eshed, spokeswoman for the custodian's office, told Reuters when asked about Katz's charge that the office would publish lists of accounts and lands under its supervision.
"The Custodian General manages assets of all sorts...It is impossible to know who perished in the Holocaust," she said.

"In the first stage, we'll publish about 10,000 names of landowners. In the next stage the names of account owners will be published so that it will be clear that it is not only money from the Holocaust," she said.

She said the lists would comprise names of absentee owners of assets. Eshed said she did not know whether that could include names of Palestinians who lost assets in Arab-Israeli wars since Israel's founding in 1948.

The spokeswoman could not put a value on the assets that would be covered in the lists nor could she say what action, if any, would be taken after the lists were published. She could not give a target date for publishing the first list.
Katz told Israel Radio the accounts were opened in the financial institutions of the Jewish settlement in then British-ruled Palestine in the 1920s and 1930s.
After World War Two, he said, unclaimed lands and accounts were held by the British Custodian General. After Israel's founding, the assets were turned over to the Jewish state.
Katz said he based his comments on reports in newspapers of the pre-state Jewish settlement and proceedings of Zionist conferences of the late 1940s.
Swiss banks have been publishing their unprecedented list in newspapers in 28 states, including Israel, and on the Internet with an eye to locating owners or heirs who could file claims.

The head of Israel's quasi-governmental Jewish Agency, Avraham Burg, serves on the independent Swiss-Jewish panel led by former U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Paul Volcker looking into charges by Jewish and other groups that the Swiss were holding Holocaust victims' money.
